html:
The mass flight of people from Darfur, in western Sudan, during the war that began there in 2003.

That year two rebel groups, the Sudan Liberation Movement and the Justice and Equality Movement, rose against a government they accused of oppressing Darfur's non-Arab peoples. The government of Omar al-Bashir answered with the army, air raids and the Janjaweed, a militia recruited mostly from Arab herding groups. Villages of the Fur, Zaghawa and Masalit peoples were burned and their people killed or driven out.

Some two million people fled their homes into camps inside Darfur, and over 200,000 crossed the border into eastern Chad. Hundreds of thousands died from violence, hunger and disease. The International Criminal Court later charged al-Bashir with genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. A joint African Union and United Nations peacekeeping force served in Darfur from 2007 to 2020. Many families stayed in the camps for twenty years, and fighting returned to Darfur in Sudan's civil war of 2023.
sum: The mass flight of people from Darfur, in western Sudan, during the war that began there in 2003.
